articles.title: 'Layer upon layer of miracles': How Nepal flood survivors were rescued from tunnel
articles.summary: From searching for a buried tunnel entrance to blowing up rocks the size of cars, rescuers had to surmount multiple challenges to reach survivors.
articles.content:
A tunnelling expert involved in the rescue operation at a blocked Nepalese hydropower tunnel has described to the BBC how they managed to reach survivors.

Arnold Dix has been advising Nepal's hydropower authorities on how to dig through the blocked tunnel to Trishuli 3A Hydropower Station, which was one of several stations hit by last week's massive flash flood on the Nepal-Tibet border.

"It's like layer upon layer of layer of miracles" that they found two men on Friday, he said, given that the multiple challenges they faced.

The first hurdle was to locate the hydropower station, in a landscape rendered nearly unrecognisable by the flood that has so far killed 1,300 people.

"I've never known an rescue operation where you had to look for an entrance of a tunnel that was previously up the hill, that was now underground. You can imagine the enormity of the avalanche, it completely buried the entrance," said Dix, who is the president of the International Tunnelling and Underground Space Association.

Using engineering techniques, old topographic maps, satellite imagery of the area after the disaster, video footage from helicopters, and "anything else we could find on the surface of the mountain such as power poles", Dix and his team triangulated the likely position of the entrance and started digging.

They found it - but the next challenge was to locate the survivors.

"We knew they would be up ahead, but we didn't know where exactly. So you just have to start digging in the right direction. And you listen out if you can hear anybody," he said.

Rescuers had to get through a tunnel blocked entirely by mud and rocks - some bigger than cars - and had to resort to using explosives to clear the way.

"We had to use explosives which we normally never do because of the risk of blowing up people [trapped in the tunnel] and blowing ourselves up," said Dix.

He credited the Nepalese army for doing "a wonderful job" in managing the explosions with precision to ensure they would not destabilise the tunnel.

At the same time, they discovered the tunnel was still full of water.

Using excavators and pumping machines, Nepalese rescuers dug a series of trenches from the tunnel all the way to the river outside, so they could drain the water.
articles.reasoning: The article describes a successful, complex rescue operation that saved survivors trapped in a blocked hydropower tunnel after a devastating flood in Nepal. The story highlights the ingenuity, bravery, and collaboration involved in overcoming extreme challenges to save lives, which has a meaningful positive impact on the affected community and is emotionally uplifting.
articles.personality_title: Rescuers overcome huge challenges to save survivors trapped in Nepal flood tunnel
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – A massive flash flood hit the Nepal-Tibet border last week, killing over 1,300 people and damaging several hydropower stations. One station’s tunnel was buried under mud and rocks, trapping workers inside.

**What happened** – Rescuers, led by tunnelling expert Arnold Dix, used maps, satellite images, and helicopter videos to find the hidden tunnel entrance buried by the avalanche. They then carefully dug through mud and large rocks, some bigger than cars, using explosives with great care to avoid harming trapped survivors. They also drained water from the tunnel by digging trenches and pumping out water.

**Impact** – Finding and rescuing the two trapped men was difficult because the tunnel entrance was buried and the tunnel was blocked and flooded. The rescue showed how teamwork, careful planning, and bravery can save lives even in very dangerous conditions. It also brought relief to a community deeply affected by the flood.

**What's next step** – The rescue team will continue clearing and repairing the tunnel and other damaged hydropower stations. Authorities will likely study this operation to improve future disaster responses and tunnel safety.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Careful planning and teamwork helped rescuers find and save survivors trapped in a buried and flooded tunnel after Nepal’s devastating flood.
articles.personality_title_fr: Les sauveteurs surmontent de grands défis pour sauver des survivants piégés dans un tunnel inondé au Népal
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Une inondation soudaine et massive a frappé la frontière Népal-Tibet la semaine dernière, causant plus de 1 300 morts et endommageant plusieurs centrales hydroélectriques. Le tunnel d’une centrale a été enterré sous la boue et des rochers, piégeant des travailleurs à l’intérieur.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Les sauveteurs, dirigés par l’expert en tunnels Arnold Dix, ont utilisé des cartes, des images satellite et des vidéos d’hélicoptère pour retrouver l’entrée du tunnel cachée par l’avalanche. Ils ont ensuite creusé avec précaution à travers la boue et de gros rochers, certains plus grands que des voitures, en utilisant des explosifs avec beaucoup de soin pour ne pas blesser les survivants piégés. Ils ont aussi drainé l’eau du tunnel en creusant des tranchées et en pompant l’eau.

**Impact** – Trouver et sauver les deux hommes piégés était difficile car l’entrée du tunnel était enterrée et le tunnel bloqué et inondé. Ce sauvetage montre comment le travail d’équipe, la planification et le courage peuvent sauver des vies même dans des conditions très dangereuses. Cela a aussi apporté un soulagement à une communauté profondément touchée par l’inondation.

**Prochaine étape** – L’équipe de secours continuera à dégager et réparer le tunnel ainsi que d’autres centrales hydroélectriques endommagées. Les autorités étudieront probablement cette opération pour améliorer les futures réponses aux catastrophes et la sécurité des tunnels.

**Résumé en une phrase** – Une planification minutieuse et un travail d’équipe ont permis aux sauveteurs de retrouver et sauver des survivants piégés dans un tunnel enterré et inondé après la dévastation causée par l’inondation au Népal.
articles.personality_title_es: Rescatistas superan grandes desafíos para salvar a sobrevivientes atrapados en un túnel inundado en Nepal
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Una inundación repentina y masiva golpeó la frontera entre Nepal y el Tíbet la semana pasada, causando más de 1,300 muertes y dañando varias centrales hidroeléctricas. El túnel de una estación quedó enterrado bajo lodo y rocas, atrapando a trabajadores dentro.

**Qué pasó** – Los rescatistas, dirigidos por el experto en túneles Arnold Dix, usaron mapas, imágenes satelitales y videos de helicópteros para encontrar la entrada oculta del túnel sepultada por la avalancha. Luego cavaron cuidadosamente a través del lodo y grandes rocas, algunas más grandes que autos, usando explosivos con mucho cuidado para no dañar a los sobrevivientes atrapados. También drenaron el agua del túnel cavando zanjas y bombeando el agua.

**Impacto** – Encontrar y rescatar a los dos hombres atrapados fue difícil porque la entrada del túnel estaba enterrada y el túnel bloqueado e inundado. El rescate mostró cómo el trabajo en equipo, la planificación cuidadosa y el valor pueden salvar vidas incluso en condiciones muy peligrosas. También trajo alivio a una comunidad profundamente afectada por la inundación.

**Próximo paso** – El equipo de rescate continuará limpiando y reparando el túnel y otras centrales hidroeléctricas dañadas. Las autoridades probablemente estudiarán esta operación para mejorar las respuestas futuras a desastres y la seguridad en túneles.

**Frase clave** – La planificación cuidadosa y el trabajo en equipo ayudaron a los rescatistas a encontrar y salvar a sobrevivientes atrapados en un túnel enterrado e inundado tras la devastadora inundación en Nepal.

articles.title: General Assembly backs creation of new UN learning institute under UN80 reforms
articles.summary: The UN General Assembly has approved the merger of two United Nations learning and training bodies, creating a new institution designed to strengthen support for both Member States and the UN system itself.
articles.content:
In a resolution adopted on Thursday, the 193-member Assembly endorsed the integration of the United Nations System Staff College (UNSSC) into the United Nations Institute for Training and Research (UNITAR) and approved the establishment of the United Nations Institute for Capability and Learning Innovation (UNICLI) from 1 January 2027.

The decision is part of the wider UN80 Initiative, that aims to make the United Nations more coherent, effective and responsive to today's challenges.

The new institute will combine UNITAR's work helping governments, diplomats and public institutions build skills and capacity with UNSSC's expertise in training, leadership development and knowledge-sharing for UN personnel.

Tweet URL

“Member States and the United Nations system are facing increasingly complex and interconnected challenges. The UN must continue to evolve, building stronger capabilities, fostering innovation, and enhancing institutional effectiveness to turn global commitments into tangible results,” said Michelle Gyles-McDonnough, UN Assistant Secretary-General and Executive Director of UNITAR.

The merger will create a single platform for learning and capability development, making it easier for Member States, UN entities and partners to access expertise and support while reducing duplication and fragmentation. Overall, the measure better equips the UN system to adapt to a rapidly changing world.

“By integrating UNSSC's and UNITAR's expertise in providing training for the UN system and Member States respectively, the new entity will be better positioned to provide a stronger, more coherent capability development function,” said Miguel Panadero, Acting Director of UNSSC.

Addressing correspondents at UN Headquarters later in the day, Spokesman Stéphane Dujarric said the Secretary-General welcomed the Assembly’s decision, “which recognizes that capability and development, continuous learning, and innovation are not ancillary functions, but strategic drivers of the UN’s effectiveness and reform, and impact for Member States.”

The UN chief invites Member States, the UN entities, partners, and all stakeholders to join “in shaping the new entity’s future and strengthening its contribution to a more sustainable, inclusive, and resilient world,” he added.

The transition will take place in phases through the end of 2026 to ensure continuity of programmes, partnerships and services. Until then, UNITAR and UNSSC will continue operating under their existing arrangements.

The new institute will be headquartered in Geneva, while Turin will continue serving as a UN learning campus and centre for leadership development. Existing offices and operations in Bonn, Hiroshima, Madrid and New York will also continue.

The merger represents one of the latest concrete actions taken by Member States under the UN80 Initiative, reflecting efforts to build a more agile and future-focused United Nations equipped to meet evolving global needs.

articles.personality_title: UN General Assembly approves new institute to improve global learning and training
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – The United Nations (UN) has two main bodies that help train people working in governments and the UN itself. These are the United Nations System Staff College (UNSSC) and the United Nations Institute for Training and Research (UNITAR). Both provide important learning and leadership programs.

**What happened** – On Thursday, the UN General Assembly, which includes all 193 member countries, agreed to merge UNSSC into UNITAR. This will create a new institute called the United Nations Institute for Capability and Learning Innovation (UNICLI). The new institute will officially start on January 1, 2027.

**Impact** – This change is part of the UN80 Initiative, a plan to make the UN work better and respond to today’s problems more quickly. By combining the two bodies, the UN will have one place to offer training and support to countries, diplomats, and UN staff. This will reduce overlap and make it easier for everyone to access important learning resources.

**What's next step** – The merger will happen gradually until the end of 2026. Until then, both UNSSC and UNITAR will keep working as they do now. The new institute will be based in Geneva, while Turin and other offices in cities like Bonn and New York will continue their roles.

**One-sentence takeaway** – The UN is creating a new learning institute by merging two existing ones to better support countries and its own staff in facing global challenges.
articles.personality_title_fr: L'Assemblée générale de l'ONU approuve la création d'un nouvel institut de formation mondiale
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Les Nations Unies disposent de deux principaux organismes qui forment les agents gouvernementaux et le personnel de l'ONU : le Collège du personnel du système des Nations Unies (UNSSC) et l'Institut des Nations Unies pour la formation et la recherche (UNITAR).

**Ce qui s'est passé** – Jeudi, l'Assemblée générale de l'ONU, composée de 193 pays membres, a décidé de fusionner l'UNSSC avec l'UNITAR. Ce nouveau centre s'appellera Institut des Nations Unies pour la capacité et l'innovation en apprentissage (UNICLI) et débutera officiellement le 1er janvier 2027.

**Impact** – Cette décision fait partie de l'initiative ONU80, qui vise à rendre l'ONU plus efficace face aux défis actuels. En réunissant ces deux organismes, l'ONU offrira un lieu unique pour la formation des pays, diplomates et employés de l'ONU, ce qui facilitera l'accès aux ressources et évitera les doublons.

**Prochaine étape** – La fusion se fera progressivement jusqu'à fin 2026. D'ici là, l'UNSSC et l'UNITAR continueront leurs activités habituelles. Le nouvel institut sera basé à Genève, tandis que Turin et d'autres bureaux comme Bonn et New York poursuivront leurs missions.

**Résumé en une phrase** – L'ONU crée un nouvel institut de formation en fusionnant deux entités pour mieux soutenir les pays et son personnel face aux défis mondiaux.
articles.personality_title_es: La Asamblea General de la ONU aprueba nuevo instituto para mejorar el aprendizaje global
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Las Naciones Unidas tienen dos organismos principales que capacitan a personas que trabajan en gobiernos y en la ONU: el Colegio del Personal del Sistema de las Naciones Unidas (UNSSC) y el Instituto de las Naciones Unidas para Formación e Investigación (UNITAR).

**Qué pasó** – El jueves, la Asamblea General de la ONU, con 193 países miembros, aprobó fusionar UNSSC dentro de UNITAR. El nuevo instituto se llamará Instituto de las Naciones Unidas para la Capacidad y la Innovación en el Aprendizaje (UNICLI) y comenzará oficialmente el 1 de enero de 2027.

**Impacto** – Esta decisión forma parte de la iniciativa UN80, que busca hacer a la ONU más efectiva frente a los problemas actuales. Al combinar ambos organismos, la ONU tendrá un solo lugar para ofrecer formación y apoyo a países, diplomáticos y personal de la ONU, facilitando el acceso y evitando duplicaciones.

**Próximo paso** – La fusión se realizará poco a poco hasta finales de 2026. Hasta entonces, UNSSC y UNITAR seguirán funcionando normalmente. El nuevo instituto tendrá su sede en Ginebra, mientras que Turín y otras oficinas en ciudades como Bonn y Nueva York seguirán con sus funciones.

**Resumen en una frase** – La ONU crea un nuevo instituto de aprendizaje al fusionar dos existentes para apoyar mejor a países y a su personal frente a desafíos globales.
